name: LFM3-VL-2B-VLD Multipass
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B (config.json max_position_embeddings 128000). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: Same tri-hybrid LFM3 text stack as LFM3-1.7B: 13 gated short-convolution layers (conv), 5 sliding-window attention layers (sliding_window 256), 6 full-attention layers at indices 2,6,10,14,18,22; GQA 16 heads / 4 KV heads, head_dim 128. Vision encoder is separate: 14 layers = 8 gated depthwise 2D convolutions interleaved with 6 bidirectional full-attention layers, 16x16 patches, spatial_merge_size 2 (each 2x2 patch block becomes one language token).
notes:
ADDED 2026-11-02 from the derivatives round (base-model query on LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B, the base of the catalog's d1-2b). A DECISION model (task=decision) built the second way: instead of a readout head it uses WebBrain's multipass VL-D protocol - a 'verify' pass that answers Yes/No per option, then a 'readout' pass that emits the option code. Text+image in (browser screenshots), per-option decisions out; nothing long-form generated.

WHAT WAS TRAINED: the vision tower was FROZEN, the language backbone was adapted with LoRA r=32/alpha=64 and merged back to BF16; a separate 'probe'/'probe-cs' variant adds trained linear decision probes on top. The model was distilled from LiquidAI/d1-2B on WebBrain multimodal browser-workflow screenshots, so the training signal is another model's decisions rather than a human-labelled capability set. config.json is the LFM3-VL-2B tri-hybrid stack unchanged (24 layers: 13 conv, 5 sliding-window at 256, 6 full attention - kv cache 0 bytes per token for the text stack since only the 6 full-attention layers hold a per-token cache and the card does not publish a combined figure), so architecture figures are inherited.

PARAMS: HF safetensors total 1,918,181,888 BF16 = 1.918B, identical to the base (LoRA merged in place). Not an MoE, so active equals total. HARDWARE GATE: passes trivially - 1.918 x 0.5 GiB = ~1 GiB at 4-bit.

EVIDENCE PROVENANCE AND HONESTY FLAGS: the benchmark is the card's OWN 'd1 Balanced Browser Decision Benchmark' (final_test split, 126 categorical questions) - it is NOT the Decision Index and is NOT on the Decision Index board, so the score is not comparable to data/decision_index.jsonl rows. The base column IS printed in the same table and is the real BF16 base checkpoint at the same protocol, so this is a genuine base-vs-tuned delta on the same test. Caveats: n=126 questions, one split, no seed count, no harness or sampling config printed, and the author both built the protocol and ran it. The 100.0% 'probe' rows are trained linear probes rather than the language model deciding, so they are deliberately not used as evidence. Much of the headline gap is in 'Unknown Recognized' (24/24 vs base 4/24) - abstention behaviour, not classification accuracy alone.

Vendor also ships GGUF/ONNX/LoRA companions (listed on the card), which is why this is runnable on the low-VRAM box despite the custom protocol.

CARD COLUMNS NOT SCORED AS ROWS: 'Completions Found' is a TIE with the base (24/24 both), and 'Unknown Recognized' is 24/24 vs base 4/24 (verify) and 0/24 (readout) on 24 items - both are raw counts, so they are recorded here in prose instead of being turned into percentages.
